status: initial design draft; not a historical workforce list or enabled runtime catalogue
setting: Canterbury 1940 simulation candidates; local existence, period titles and legal/training requirements require review
policy: Five draft roles per family are a starting scaffold; review may introduce branches, merge or remove stages.
Roles are posts with duties and capacity, not universal seniority levels. Management, ownership, licensing and ordination are distinct gates.
No automatic career promotion, skill award, employment, qualification, authority, business ownership or population allocation.
Training consumes mentor capacity and native time; mentor loss suspends training safely.
Allow laterally transferable skills only through explicit reviewed links; professions and religious traditions are not interchangeable.
Children, students outside workplace training, homemakers, retired residents, unemployed and unavailable residents have activity statuses, not compulsory jobs.
Age, consent, safety, role-specific training, wages, shifts, funded vacancies, premises and reachable routes must be configured before activation.
Transport roles do not activate reference-only rail or create unsupported fleets. Religious roles do not assert local historical staffing or override institution closures.
Draft titles reflect a proposed period vocabulary, not gender restrictions or verified historical rank structures.
